backlog.title: pi-interrogator v1.0 — structured interrogation extension for pi
backlog.description: Build the complete pi-interrogator extension per spec/: one non-blocking `interrogate` tool (upsert/read/reopen/answers), a persistent replace-editor answer panel (short form, deep view, overview, gate dimming, ripple confirms, sacred drafts), delta-based submissions that trigger agent replies, rev+epoch staleness guards, auto-close on agent_settled with one-time completion injection, suspend/resume ecosystem with widget, branch-correct persistence/reconstruction, non-TUI fallback, and full config/remappable keymaps. Greenfield TypeScript package loaded by pi 0.85.1 via jiti. Research findings: plan/001_0d6760db6bc5/architecture/ (pi-api-validation.md, reference-patterns.md, environment-and-conflicts.md, system-context.md, external-deps.md).

milestones.title: Tool + state core (no UI)
milestones.description: PRD M1 (h2.48): scaffold the package, config loader, the full state engine (state machine, merge rules, rev/epoch, snapshots, dependsOn evaluator), and the interrogate tool with schema, guards, caps, read formatting, non-TUI fallback digest, and tool-row renderers. Ends runnable: model upserts/reads in a scratch session; guards reject stale calls; caps truncate with warnings; details carry full state.

tasks.title: State engine (state.ts)

subtasks.title: InterrogationState core: types, map/order, rev/epoch, change events
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: state.ts never touches UI; emits change events consumed by panel/widget/renderers (h2.13). Node EventEmitter suffices. Never cache state across session_shutdown (h2.43).
2. INPUT: scaffold from P1.M1.T1.S1.
3. LOGIC: export types per h2.17: QuestionStatus = open|answered|submitted|reasked|moot|withdrawn|closed; Question {id, title?, prompt, description?, type: choice|text, options?: {value,label,ramification?}[], recommendation?, group?, gate?, dependsOn?: {id,equals?,notEquals?}[], rev, status, answer?: {value, text?, at}}; InterrogationState class {goal, epoch (starts 1), questions: Map<string,Question>, order: string[], snapshots: Snapshot[]} with: createInterrogationState(), upsert entry points (applied by S2), bumpRev(id), bumpEpoch(), getQuestion, orderedQuestions, groupSummaries, serialize() -> plain JSON (details-compatible) and static deserialize(). Emit events: 'changed', 'questions-upserted', 'epoch-bumped', 'completed-cleared'. rev starts 1 per question; user answers do NOT bump rev (h2.39).
4. OUTPUT: state singleton accessor + serialize/deserialize consumed by tool.ts details (P1.M1.T3.S4), persistence mirror (P1.M7.T1.S1), reconstruction (P1.M7.T1.S2), panel rendering.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on InterrogationState documenting the status machine diagram from h2.38.

subtasks.title: Merge rules 1-4 + status transitions
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: merge rules are the contract the model relies on for re-asks; withdrawal keeps the question in the map for audit (h2.38, Q34=A).
2. INPUT: InterrogationState from P1.M1.T2.S1.
3. LOGIC: implement applyUpsert(incoming: Question[], ctx) per h2.21 by id: (1) same option values -> silent text/description/ramification update, answer kept, rev+1; (2) changed options -> answer reset, status reasked, rev+1 (panel draft preserved — drafts live panel-side, state must not clear them; expose questionRevBumped event so panel knows); (3) new id -> appended, status open, rev 1; (4) existing id omitted -> status withdrawn, kept in map with reason. Also: user answer path markAnswered(id, answer) -> status answered(pending); markSubmitted(ids) -> submitted; closeSubmitted(ids) -> closed(archived); editing a closed answer re-marks answered(pending) (FR-2, Q24=B). Withdraw/moot are terminal-until-re-upsert; re-upsert of withdrawn id with rev+1 reopens per h2.38.
4. OUTPUT: applyUpsert + transition methods consumed by tool.ts (P1.M1.T3.S1), auto-close (P1.M2.T2.S1), panel submit flush, reconstruction replay (P1.M7.T1.S2).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on applyUpsert enumerating the 4 rules verbatim from h2.21.

subtasks.title: dependsOn evaluator + transitive ripple closure
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: conditions evaluate locally and instantly (FR-17); ripple = transitive closure over reverse dependsOn edges (Q39=B, defaulted decision — user may veto, keep the UX exactly as specified).
2. INPUT: Question.dependsOn shape from P1.M1.T2.S1; current answers.
3. LOGIC: export evaluateDependsOn(state): for each question with dependsOn, condition met iff every {id, equals?, notEquals?} is satisfied by the dependency's current answer (unanswered dependency = unmet unless no condition given); unmet -> status moot with reason string like `moot: storage=sqlite` (h2.29 overview format); re-met -> back to open (h2.38). Export computeRipple(state, changedId): transitive set of question ids whose dependsOn chain (any depth) passes through changedId and would newly unmet — used by the FR-18 confirm to list answered/submitted victims only. Idempotent; cheap; callable after every answer change and after reconstruction.
4. OUTPUT: evaluateDependsOn + computeRipple consumed by panel ripple confirm (P1.M5.T4.S1), overview moot markers (P1.M5.T2.S1), reconstruction step 5 (P1.M7.T1.S2).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on computeRipple with a 3-level transitive example.

subtasks.title: Snapshot ring + diff computation
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: snapshots power diff cards and post-hoc recovery; NOT user-facing undo in v1 (h2.39). Bounded ring of 10.
2. INPUT: InterrogationState from P1.M1.T2.S1.
3. LOGIC: snapshot() on every submission (before epoch bump), keep last 10. Export computeDiff(prev, next): {changed: [{id, title, from, to}][]} where from/to are answer value/label summaries and edited-archived answers appear with `(changed)` marker data (AC-13). Also digestSince(epochFrom): compact one-line-per-submission delta digest used in stale-guard rejection messages (h3.8 'Changes since epoch N').
4. OUTPUT: computeDiff + digestSince consumed by delivery delta builder (P1.M2.T1.S1), stale guards (P1.M1.T3.S2), submission card renderer (P1.M7.T3.S1).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on computeDiff documenting the SubmissionCardData shape {changed[], note?, epoch, remainOpen}.

subtasks.title: Schema + action routing + validation
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: use `import { Type } from 'typebox'` (bare — pi 0.85.1 dep, NOT @sinclair/typebox) and `StringEnum` from @earendil-works/pi-ai for the type enum (Google compat) — see external-deps.md.

Route four action shapes per h2.20: questions present -> upsert; empty object -> read; reopen:true -> reopen; answers present -> record (non-TUI only, ignored in TUI). Validate: type=choice requires options with unique values; recommendation must match an option value; ids non-empty; question count <= caps.questions (truncate-with-warning, never reject, per h2.23).
4. OUTPUT: exported parseInterrogateParams(args) + action discriminator consumed by P1.M1.T3.S2-S5 and debug commands (P1.M2.T3.S1).

subtasks.title: rev/epoch stale guards (throw with current state)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: pi sets isError ONLY when execute THROWS (pi-api-validation.md, extensions.md:2068). The rejection message must carry current state so the model self-heals in one round trip (AC-8).
2. INPUT: parsed params from P1.M1.T3.S1; state revs/epoch from P1.M1.T2.S1; digestSince from P1.M1.T2.S4.
3. LOGIC: upsert touching existing question ids requires each question's current rev (param rev) AND top-level epoch matching session epoch; answers[] requires epoch. On mismatch throw Error with message exactly shaped per h3.8: `STALE: {id} is at rev {n} (you sent {m}); session epoch is {e} (you sent {x}). Current {id}: {text}. Changes since epoch {x}: {delta digest}. Re-apply against current state.` Read ({}) is never guarded. Guards apply in both TUI and non-TUI.
4. OUTPUT: guard functions consumed by upsert + answers paths (P1.M1.T3.S1 routing); verified by AC-8.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on the guard explaining throw-to-isError semantics for future maintainers.

subtasks.title: Caps engine: formula, truncation warnings
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: soft caps only — over-budget content truncates with an explicit warning in the tool result, NEVER a hard reject (h2.23). ctx.model.contextWindow is accessible in tool execute ctx (pi-api-validation.md).
2. INPUT: config caps from P1.M1.T1.S2; question batch from params.
3. LOGIC: export applyCaps(questions, goal, config, contextWindow): per-question description <= max(cap.description, budget/questionCount) chars where totalDescriptionBudget = min(contextBudgetPct/100 x contextWindow x 4 chars-per-token, 60000); ramification <= cap.ramification; options truncated to cap.options (keep recommendation); questions hard-listed at cap.questions count with warning; goal <= cap.goal. Return {questions, goal, warnings: string[]} with warnings like `q7 description truncated at 2100 chars — restructure if essential`.
4. OUTPUT: applyCaps consumed by upsert path; warnings appended to result text (P1.M1.T3.S4).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on applyCaps with the formula and config override names.

subtasks.title: Submission delta builder
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:

2. INPUT: computeDiff output + batchNote from P1.M1.T2.S4; epoch from state.

subtasks.title: sendMessage plumbing: triggerTurn + streaming delivery
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: pi.sendMessage does NOT trigger an agent reply by default — CRITICAL: pass options {triggerTurn: true, deliverAs: 'followUp'}; when the agent is streaming at submit time use deliverAs 'steer' (pi-api-validation.md §Mismatch 2, TD types.d.ts:971-981). Custom messages are role custom and DO participate in LLM context (model sees the delta).
2. INPUT: message object from P1.M2.T1.S1; registered tool from P1.M1.T3.S6.
3. LOGIC: export deliverSubmission(pi, msg): pi.sendMessage(msg, ctx.isIdle?.() === false ? {deliverAs: 'steer'} : {triggerTurn: true, deliverAs: 'followUp'}). Verify with ctx.isIdle()/mode guards. No tool call ever waits on the user (commitment 1) — this is the only turn-triggering path.
4. OUTPUT: deliverSubmission consumed by panel ctrl+s (P1.M3.T2.S2 via lifecycle) and debug submit (P1.M2.T3.S1).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on deliverSubmission explaining triggerTurn semantics.

tasks.title: lifecycle.ts — auto-close and completion trigger
tasks.description: Per-run upsert tracking via tool_execution events, close pass on agent_settled, one-time completion injection with panel-dismiss hook.

subtasks.title: Auto-close engine (agent_settled close pass)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: event ordering risk (h2.51) is handled by per-run flags: args arrive on tool_execution_start (pi-api-validation.md §Events), result on tool_execution_end {toolCallId, toolName, result, isError}. agent_settled abort semantics are UNDOCUMENTED — verify empirically with a scripted abort and keep the close pass idempotent (pi-api-validation.md §Unknown 1).
2. INPUT: state transitions closeSubmitted/markReasked from P1.M1.T2.S2; registered tool from P1.M1.T3.S6.
3. LOGIC: implement h2.44 algorithm exactly: on submission delivery set submittedRun=false; on tool_execution_start/end for interrogate with questions action, mark each touched submitted question reasked and submittedRun=true; on agent_settled: for each q submitted-at-current-epoch, if not reasked this run -> status closed(archived); aborted runs count as settled (agent_settled fires). Subscribe in index.ts. Expose lifecycle.onPanelDismiss hook (no-op until M3) so completion can dismiss the panel later.
4. OUTPUT: close-pass engine consumed by completion trigger (P1.M2.T2.S2); proves AC-3 state semantics.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on the auto-close algorithm including the abort caveat.

subtasks.title: Completion trigger + one-time injection
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: completion fires when the last open question closes after an agent_settled with no re-ask (FR-5); injection uses the same sendMessage options contract as submissions but must NOT triggerTurn if the agent is mid-reply — deliver via followUp (P1.M2.T1.S2 plumbing).
2. INPUT: close pass from P1.M2.T2.S1; buildCompletion from P1.M2.T1.S3; deliverSubmission from P1.M2.T1.S2.
3. LOGIC: after each close pass, if no questions remain in {open, reasked, answered, submitted, moot}: deliver completion message ONCE (guard with a completed flag on state), invoke lifecycle.onPanelDismiss() (stub here, real panel in P1.M3.T1.S1), clear in-memory state but KEEP session entries for audit (h3.9). Edge per h2.37: 0 open + pending submissions -> completion waits until close pass after the next agent reply.
4. OUTPUT: completion flow consumed by panel (dismiss) and AC-14; entry audit trail preserved for renderers (P1.M7.T3.S2).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on the completion invariant (fires exactly once).
